title: Directional Terms, Body Planes, and Body Cavities

sections.learningObjectives:
- Define the standard anatomical position and apply the directional terms superior, inferior, anterior (ventral), posterior (dorsal), medial, lateral, proximal, and distal.
- Identify the major body planes (sagittal, midsagittal, parasagittal, coronal/frontal, transverse, and oblique) and the portions of the body each divides.
- Identify the major body cavities (cranial, spinal, thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic) and the structures each protects.
- Apply directional terms, body planes, and body cavities together to locate structures and interpret basic documentation.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of a toy soldier standing straight with hands open and palms showing forward. Everyone agrees on this starting pose so words like left, right, front, and back mean the same thing every time.

### Question 2

Show your palms like you are saying stop. Your palms point the same way your face points, which is the front.

### Question 3

It is like agreeing which way is up on a map so everyone reads the same map the same way, no matter which way they are facing.

### Question 4

Front still means the same side of the body even when you lie down. On your back, your belly-button side points up at the ceiling.

### Question 5

When you hold your hands out with palms up, your thumbs stick out to the sides, away from the middle of your body.

### Question 6

Your feet stand side by side like two straight lines, both pointing the same way you are looking.

### Question 7

Lie on your tummy and your back is up in the air. Back is the dorsal side, so dorsal faces up.

### Question 8

Arms hang down like a soldier at attention, but with the hands turned so the palms face forward.

### Question 9

Superior means above, like the top shelf is above the bottom shelf. Your head is superior to your feet.

### Question 10

Inferior means below, like the bottom shelf is below the top one. Your feet are inferior to your head.

### Question 11

Anterior is the front, like the front door of a house. Your face and chest are on the anterior side.

### Question 12

Posterior is the back, like the back yard of a house. Your shoulder blades are on the posterior side.

### Question 13

Medial is toward the middle, like the center line of a road. Your nose is medial because it is near the middle of your face.

### Question 14

Lateral is toward the side, like the shoulder of a road is to the side of the center line.

### Question 15

Proximal means closer to where something attaches, like the part of a leash closest to your hand. Your shoulder is proximal because it is close to where your arm attaches.

### Question 16

Distal means farther from where something attaches, like the end of a leash farthest from your hand. Your fingers are distal because they are far from where your arm attaches.

### Question 17

Think of the leg as a road from your hip to your toes. The knee is an earlier stop, closer to the hip, so it is proximal to the ankle.

### Question 18

On the road from your shoulder to your fingers, the elbow comes before the wrist, so the elbow is proximal.

### Question 19

The nose is in the middle of the face, so it is medial. The ears are on the sides, so they are lateral.

### Question 20

The breastbone is like a shield in front of your heart, so it is anterior to the heart.

### Question 21

Your spine is in your back and your windpipe is in front, so the spine is posterior to the windpipe.

### Question 22

Your forehead is higher than your mouth, so it is superior to the mouth.

### Question 23

The fingers are at the far end of the arm, away from the shoulder, so they are distal to the wrist.

### Question 24

The shoulder is where the arm starts, closest to the body, so it is proximal to the elbow.

### Question 25

Proximal and distal are for arms and legs, like saying closer to or farther from where the limb plugs into the body.

### Question 26

Proximal means closer to where a limb attaches, so it does not make sense to use it on the trunk itself. The trunk uses plain up and down instead.

### Question 27

Your knee is lower down your leg than your hip, so the knee is inferior to the hip.

### Question 28

Hold your palms forward and your pinkies are nearest the middle of your body, so the pinky is medial.

### Question 29

Your eyes are on the sides and your nose is in the middle, so the eyes are lateral to the nose.

### Question 30

The heart is in the middle of the chest with a lung on each side, so the heart is medial to the lungs.

### Question 31

Anterior and ventral are two names for the same idea: the front. It is like calling a couch both a couch and a sofa.

### Question 32

Your chin is lower than your nose, so the chin is inferior to the nose.

### Question 33

Imagine a giant knife slicing you from front to back, making a right side and a left side. That is a sagittal cut.

### Question 34

A midsagittal cut goes exactly down the middle, like cutting a sandwich in half so both sides match.

### Question 35

Para means beside, so a parasagittal cut is beside the middle, making one side bigger than the other.

### Question 36

A coronal cut is like a front-to-back slice that separates your front half from your back half.

### Question 37

A transverse cut is a flat slice across the body, like cutting a loaf of bread into top and bottom pieces.

### Question 38

Axial is just another word for a flat slice across the body, the kind that separates top from bottom.

### Question 39

To split something into a top part and a bottom part, you cut across it, which is the transverse plane.

### Question 40

A cut that separates your front from your back is the coronal plane, like the seam that splits a shirt into its front and back panels.

### Question 41

A cut that gives you a right piece and a left piece runs along the sagittal plane, like splitting a person into two side-by-side halves.

### Question 42

Two of the planes stand up like walls (sagittal and coronal), and one lies flat like a tabletop (transverse).

### Question 43

Corona means crown. A crown sits on your head from front to back, which is why the front-and-back plane is called coronal.

### Question 44

An oblique cut is a slanted slice, like cutting a sandwich on a diagonal instead of straight across.

### Question 45

Axial slices are like stacking a loaf of bread and looking at each flat slice from the top, which is the transverse plane.

### Question 46

A sagittal picture of the brain is like slicing it down the middle so you see a right side and a left side.

### Question 47

Your breastbone is in front and your spine is in back, so a front-versus-back cut (coronal) would put them on opposite sides.

### Question 48

The dorsal cavity is the back cavity, holding your brain up top and your spinal cord down the back.

### Question 49

The ventral cavity is the front cavity, holding your heart and lungs up top and your belly organs below.

### Question 50

The cranial cavity is the hard helmet space inside your skull that holds your brain.

### Question 51

The spinal cavity is the tunnel down your backbone that protects the cord that carries messages to and from your brain.

### Question 52

The thoracic cavity is your chest space, where the heart and the two lungs live.

### Question 53

Each lung has its own protective pocket, the pleural cavity, inside the chest.

### Question 54

The mediastinum is the middle hallway of the chest, with a lung room on each side.

### Question 55

The abdominal cavity is your belly space, holding the organs that digest food.

### Question 56

The pelvic cavity is the lowest front space, holding the bladder and reproductive organs.

### Question 57

The abdominal and pelvic cavities flow into each other like two connected rooms with no wall between them.

### Question 58

The brain and spinal cord are one long cord, so their protective spaces connect like a single tunnel from head to lower back.

### Question 59

The pleura is the slick wrapper around each lung that lets it slide as you breathe.

### Question 60

The peritoneum is the smooth lining that wraps your belly organs so they can slide past each other.

### Question 61

Your stomach is in your belly, which is the abdominal cavity.

### Question 62

Your bladder sits low in your pelvis, in the pelvic cavity.

### Question 63

Your liver is tucked up high on the right side of your belly, in the right upper quadrant.

### Question 64

The pericardial cavity is the heart's own little water-filled pocket, so a problem there is a heart problem.

### Question 65

The mediastinum sits in the middle, with a lung pocket on each side, so it is medial to the pleural cavities.

### Question 66

Your appendix is down low on the right side, in the right lower quadrant.

### Question 67

Your skull space is in the back half of your body, so the cranial cavity belongs to the dorsal cavity.

### Question 68

The diaphragm is the divider: the heart is above it and the stomach is below it, so the heart is superior.

### Question 69

When you breathe in, the diaphragm muscle pushes down to make the chest space bigger, like pulling a plunger down to make more room.

### Question 70

The brain and spinal cord are one long cord, so their protective tunnel is one long space: the dorsal cavity.

### Question 71

Superior means toward your head no matter how you are lying, just like the top of a photo stays the top even if you turn the photo sideways.

### Question 72

Each organ has its own named wrapper: the heart has the pericardium, the lungs have the pleura, and the belly organs have the peritoneum.

### Question 73

Your chest cavity is above your belly cavity, so the thoracic cavity is superior.

### Question 74

Up high on the left side of your belly, above and to the side of your belly button, sits the spleen.
